## Environment fingerprint

- Framework `objectstack-ai/objectstack` main @ **`c4196099`**, the release tip, built in its own git worktree beside part A's 8e3d4a54 tree so neither run touched the other: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build --concurrency=2`, `pnpm console:build` (`✓ @objectstack/console dist ready (85560 KB) from ui/apps/console`), showcase compiled once (10:02–10:13Z). Delta on top of 8e3d4a54: c4196099 (#33075), b2322209 (#32931), 9df85e1d (#33076), e003ebbe (#33068), d60a0de3 (pm tooling, no product surface).
- Boots `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin --no-compile --no-watch -p PORT -d file:/tmp/qa3/C/<runner>/<db>` with `OS_PORT` / `OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT` exported, stopped by process group; vite console dev servers on their own ports; installs and scratch plugins from scratch copies symlinked to the c4196099 tree; `examples/app-showcase/.objectstack/installed-packages` absent and `git status` clean at the end. Ports 41300–41359.
- Special boots: a SCIM-enabled boot (`OS_SCIM_ENABLED=true`, credential minted through `admin/scim/mint-credential`); phone + two-factor on, and `NODE_ENV=production` with phone on (SMS_SERVICE_REQUIRED); zero-user with sign-up disabled; walled `isolated` invite-only and `group`; a scratch copy registering a local OIDC provider through `applyConfigPatch` with `OS_SSO_ENABLED=true` and its origin in `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, beside a local SMTP sink; `OS_OIDC_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false`; open audience posture with `member_default` (email verification); a default boot and a scheduled-work-on boot of a scratch copy (flow-status).
- Execution: Tier 1 pins run centrally at c4196099 (sequential vitest `--maxWorkers=1`, 6 groups): **605 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Tier 2 by 3 runner subagents (effort high): approvals/automation/forms/studio (9), identity-auth (9, #33075 first), identity-auth (7).
- **Container restart at ≈10:21Z** (the machine was reclaimed; files restored from checkpoint). Every live boot ended; runners resumed at 10:28Z, re-booting on the same DB files where they reused one (noted per item — the dynamic-approver-routing paused run survived and was decided on the second boot). No clause is scored on a half-run leg.
- Timestamps (UTC): build 10:02–10:13; pins 10:14–10:17; runners 10:14–10:53 (setup ≈14 runner-minutes, testing ≈84 runner-minutes, ≈10 lost to the restart).

## The delta, driven live

- **#33075 (c4196099) — a directory deactivation revokes the user's API keys, and no one restores them: holds.** SCIM credential minted (`Cache-Control: no-store`); users provisioned through `POST /api/v1/auth/scim/v2/Users` (`source: idp_provisioned`), given a local password, each minting keys that read 200. Five deactivation spellings — SCIM PATCH `active:false`, `DELETE /Users/{id}`, PUT `active:false`, Azure-style pathless PATCH `{active:false}`, and the string `"False"` — each stamp every key row `revoked:true, revoked_reason: scim_deactivated` (an owner-revoked key is restamped) and the next request is refused **403 `API_KEY_REVOKED`** (the ruled #23367 shape; only an unknown key is 401) naming the new-key road; every session row is deleted, the old bearer reads 401, sign-in answers 403 `BANNED_USER` `details.cause: scim_deactivated`. Re-activation (SCIM PATCH `active:true`, a SCIM re-POST re-linking through the tombstone, and `import-users` upsert) lifts the ban only: every old key stays revoked. Every restore door refuses — owner and admin `restore_api_key` 403, owner and admin PATCH `{revoked:false}` (with or without `revoked_reason:null`) 403, `revoked_reason` not editable 403, `service-account/restore-key` 404. A later admin set-user-password restamps only unrevoked keys (`admin_password_reset`) and leaves `scim_deactivated` rows as they are. A key minted after re-activation reads 200 and only the owner's rows; two other users' keys read 200 after every step. Control: an admin ban does not share the revocation (by design per the commit) — the key reads 401 while banned, its row stays `revoked:false`, and it works again after unban. A wrong SCIM bearer and a member's session bearer are both 401.
- **#33076 (9df85e1d) — MCP recall / resubmit by the submitter's agent: holds.** `list_actions` lists approve/reject/reassign/send_back/recall/resubmit on sys_approval_request, each aiExposed and requiresConfirmation. Recall: non-submitter unconfirmed 428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, confirmed 403 "Only the person who submitted this approval request can recall it…" (still pending, no action row); submitter unconfirmed 428 (nothing recorded), confirmed → recalled with exactly one [recall, Mei] row. Resubmit on a returned request: non-participant 404 REQUEST_NOT_FOUND; submitter unconfirmed 428, confirmed → round 2 pending, the run completes after approval; a participant on another pending request: resubmit 409 INVALID_STATE, recall 403.
- **#33068 (e003ebbe) — the flow answer names read-only fields dropped in map items and resumed subflow children: holds.** On invoice `tax_rate` (readonlyWhen on paid invoices): the map answer carries `droppedFields [{object: showcase_invoice, fields: [tax_rate], reason: readonly_when}]` folded once, value unchanged; a resumed subflow child carries the same entry whether the resume names the parent or the child run id, and the parent's subflow step carries it; a draft-invoice control has no droppedFields member. (A static readonly write is refused at registration, 422 flow-update-readonly-field, so the probe needs a readonlyWhen field.)
- **#32931 (b2322209)** is plugin-form's modal/drawer holder pick; no C-browser item drives it directly beyond form-dirty-guard (pins green, live legs pass). The C-api slice carries its items.

## Fails — reproduction rule and disposition

**approvals.record-page-decisions · A4** — stale spec, existing re-point card `card-p2-1.md` (unchanged since ee9ad834). A contributor-bound member who reads project `tyLQ-4kFq15pIZCu` but is not a participant of its pending exec_review request: `POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/areq_e4d9df94…/approve {}` twice → 404 `{"code":"REQUEST_NOT_FOUND"}`, request stays pending; the clause expects 403 FORBIDDEN. The read gate holds (the member's approvals read is empty, the page draws 0 declared actions); the override-menu half passes.

**studio-authoring.flow-status-matches-runtime · A1** — stale spec, existing re-point card `card-browser-5.md`. A writable package's schedule flow (interval 60000) on a default boot: `_status` reason "disabled by deployment policy — …" with `unboundCause: deployment_policy`; the rail and header titles read the console's worded sentence ("This deployment keeps scheduled work that comes with a package switched off…") and the verbatim reason is the Problems note's hover title, by design in `describeFlowRunStatus` (flow-problems.ts). Two page loads.

## Off-clause probes (rule 8)

Each runner kept a probe budget after every item (2–10 min, the #33075 and #33076 drives inside it); per-item minutes and doors are in the probe log (record-C-browser-clauses-1.md). No product defect found; no card drafted.

Observed and not carded (low, for the seat to weigh): a cross-user unlink by a caller holding a single account answers `FAILED_TO_UNLINK_LAST_ACCOUNT` (the last-account check runs before ownership — misleading wording, row untouched); cross-user OAuth `get-consent` / `delete-consent` answer 401 rather than 403/404; an `import-users` upsert overwrites a directory-managed user's name; setting a SCIM user's password moves `sys_user.source` from `idp_provisioned` to `env_native`; on the unbound schedule flow the header enable switch is green "Switched on" beside "Not running here"; a flow authored `status:'draft'` is enabled and bound (by design per the boot log — "Created Off" means `obsolete`); approval / wait / screen steps log `success` while the run reads `paused`; an OIDC provider's overflow menu also offers "Edit SAML Settings"; the admin `revoked` sessions view keeps the subtitle "Active user sessions". An operator-registered OIDC provider asserting a verified address implicitly links and signs in to that user, platform admin included — the item's A1 design (a trusted provider vouching for a verified address), recorded, not scored.

## Parked-on #32908

Fixture gaps: SSO just-in-time sign-in plus SCIM deactivation (SCIM adopts an SSO account only on a verified domain, which needs a DNS TXT record — `OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION`); the auth-method-matrix S4 SSO half and S5 device variant; magic-link / passkeys UI (objectui#4179 not_planned); users from admin create-user carry `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED` on every data read until they change their password — fixtures should say to clear it; a local OIDC provider needs its origin in `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` (else 400 SSO_REGISTER_FAILED "not publicly routable"); the showcase self-ping connector dials :3000 on a `--no-compile` boot (flow-node-type-matrix connector ping).

Per-item checklist-accuracy notes follow.

**approvals.inbox-metadata-actions**
- A1.verify: "the dev admin on that same pending request shows 'Override Recall'" holds only once the admin's own slot on EXP-2001 is spent (the fixture routes the admin's manager group there); with the slot open the label is plain "Recall" (approvalOverride.ts isOverrideDecision, override-only viewer). Measured both states.
- A3.verify names /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id/approve|remind as the click's network literal; the console posts /api/v1/actions/sys_approval_request/approval_* (action door, objectstack#27611), which forwards to that route. Stale literal, not a defect.

**approvals.dynamic-approver-routing**
- S3 says the inbox row navigates to /apps/APP/sys_approval_request/record/ID: confirmed (APP = com.example.showcase).
- The run's step log shows co_sign [approval] with status 'success' while the run reads 'paused' (both chains). This was noted, not scored: the clause reads run status, which is correct.

**approvals.record-page-decisions**
- S5/S6/A1/A2 name POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id/reject|approve as the wire. The bar posts the action door POST /api/v1/actions/sys_approval_request/approval_reject|approval_approve, with recordId = the request id and the comment under params.comment. Stale literal; the substance holds.
- S2 "capture the read the bar ran on: GET /api/v1/approvals/requests?object=…&recordId=…": on first load the approvals arrive inside POST /api/v1/data/showcase_project/:id/page. The GET fires on the post-decision refresh. Read the viewer block directly.
- S9's example budget (200000 on a fourth project) can trip the showcase's 120%-of-spend validation rule on Data Platform (spent 420000), which answers 400. Pick a budget above spent/1.2.
- The member's page logs 404 GET /api/v1/meta/object/sys_business_unit and /sys_comment_reaction. This is not scored (same class as the #32955 family, already known from earlier rounds).

**automation.flow-node-type-matrix**
- S8 composite run screenshot (Studio Runs tab, showcase_fan_out_notify run_8e24b4c8): 'Failed', run-level error "Node 'fan_out' failed: parallel 'fan_out': branch failed — …", 'FAILURE Notify in parallel PARALLEL', nested '↳ BRANCH 1 SUCCESS Notify Owner NOTIFY' and '↳ BRANCH 2 FAILURE Slack Notify HTTP … ENOTFOUND hooks.slack.com'.
- showcase_declarative_connector_ping (fired by every task create) fails `connector_action(showcase_status_api.request) failed: fetch failed` on this --no-compile boot: its frozen base URL dials :3000, which matches the known environment note. Not scored; connector_action was proven on two other connector flows.
- The bogus-node trigger answers HTTP **400** with success:false. The clause names only success:false, which holds.
- The run step log records approval/wait/screen steps with status 'success' while the run is 'paused' (e.g. dynamic approval co_sign, hold [wait]). The suspension is read from run status, as A2 does.

**identity-auth.phone-signin-surfaces**
- On the OFF boot the Email label carries "*" (required). On ON it does not, because a phone can stand in for it ("Required when no email is given"). This is consistent with the product.

**identity-auth.auth-method-matrix**
- /auth/config wraps its payload in `data` ({success, data:{emailPassword, features…}}). The steps read `features.*` as top level.
- Also served under the prefix: GET /api/v1/auth/.well-known/openid-configuration → 200. A8 says the documents are "mounted at app root, not the /api/v1/auth prefix". Both answer, and the root one is the RFC location. This is a note only.
- On a dev boot, phoneNumberOtp is advertised true with no SMS service (the log transport). S3 already explains this.

**identity-auth.admin-lifecycle-operations**
- During impersonation, the admin's ORIGINAL bearer answers 401 on get-session and on data reads. The held session is refused, so a second admin session was needed to read sys_session.impersonated_by. S9 could say so.
- S10's "a throwaway that OWNS a showcase row": showcase_task needs `project` (400 VALIDATION_FAILED otherwise).
- On the single posture, create-user answers membershipCreated:false even though the user lands in the Default Organization's member list. That is the bootstrap join, not create-user's.

**identity-auth.session-list-revoke**
- A0's "BOTH of A's sessions" assumes A holds exactly two. Here, user setup (create-user, then a forced change-password needing a sign-in) left A extra live sessions, so the count was 5, all A's own. Either start from a user with no prior sign-ins, or read the clause as "A's sessions only".
- The admin `revoked` view keeps the object's subtitle "Active user sessions" and the "Sign out other devices" toolbar button. This is cosmetic.

**identity-auth.api-key-ui-lifecycle**
- S4/S5 call the row action a `PATCH … bodyExtra {revoked:true}`. The console's row action actually posts to POST /api/v1/actions/sys_api_key/revoke_api_key (and restore_api_key) with {recordId, params:{}}. The PATCH door also works, and both were driven. Re-spell the step, or name both doors.
- A user made by admin/create-user is mustChangePassword:true, so every data read answers 403 PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED until change-password. The fixture should say to clear that first.
- Off-clause: the row menu offers "Edit" on sys_api_key, yet a PATCH of `name` is refused 403 "None of the submitted fields (name) are editable … Editable fields: revoked". This was not opened in the UI form, so it is a note only.

**identity-auth.org-membership-team-management**
- S6 says remove-member revokes the live sessions. Measured: the old session answers 401 at once, with reason organization_membership_ended. The step is correct.
- A1's "the gated operation" is not named. invite-member worked as a discriminator for member ↔ admin. Suggest naming it.

**identity-auth.oauth-app-consent-loop**
- create-client's default grant_types is [authorization_code] only; A3's "access/refresh tokens" needs grant_types including refresh_token AND the offline_access scope at authorize. Without them the token answer has no refresh_token. The step could say so.
- Cross-user get-consent / delete-consent answer 401 (not 403/404); a refusal either way, noted only.

**identity-auth.linked-accounts-social**
- The UI unlink goes through the action door POST /api/v1/actions/sys_account/unlink_account (which reaches the auth unlink), not a direct POST /auth/unlink-account from the browser; the step text names the latter. The direct door also works (implicit-linking run: 200 {status:true}).
- Fixture: a real social provider still needs real client credentials; the local OIDC provider stood in (as rev 5 records).

**identity-auth.identity-import-wizard**
- The wizard's default match mode is "Always create new"; S4's upsert needs the operator to pick "Update if matched, else create" and tick Match on: Email (the Import button stays disabled until a match field is chosen). The step could say so.
- An insert-mode import of an existing email answers row error "User already exists. Use another email." (IMPORT_ROW_FAILED) inside a 200. That is correct, recorded for the item's negatives.

**identity-auth.first-run-owner-bootstrap**
- Same as the earlier run: S5 says "two document loads, to /_console/ and then /_console/home", but both document requests were /_console/, and /home is a client route after the reload. The contract (a full-document exit) holds.

**identity-auth.self-signup-gate**
- As before, the invitation card heading is "Dev Admin invited you to join Default Organization", not "Accept your invitation". The link is as described.

**identity-auth.workspace-org-switch**
- A5's "the UI surfaces an error" has no UI path: the forged call is API-only, and after it the console shows the organization picker (no active org), not an error. Scored on "never the foreign org".
- The admin persona note says the walled admin "starts with none"; at c4196099 the seeded admin already holds a "Default Organization" on a walled boot. create-user still needs the admin's active org set to the intended one.
- A3's group write needs a project in the new org (showcase_task.project is required); the member's own org is seeded, so a Beta project exists.

**identity-auth.sso-provider-groups-claim**
- fixtures.knownGaps is right that the issuer must be reachable; a local IdP additionally needs its origin in OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS (the register door refuses a loopback discovery URL otherwise). Worth adding to the item's requires.
- Observed: the OIDC provider's overflow menu also offers "Edit SAML Settings". Not scored; cosmetic.

**integration-system.flow-connector-picker**
- A fixture flow for POST /api/v1/automation must declare a `connectorConfig` block on the node (connectorId/actionId/input). A `config:{connectorId…}` form is refused 422 INVALID_METADATA "a `connector_action` node requires a `connectorConfig` block". The item's fixture text does not say this.
- By design (connector-input-fields.ts), the typed form shows no required asterisk for echo_upper's `text`, though the JSON-Schema `required` lists it. Noted so A2's "input fields match inputSchema" is not read as a gap.

**records-forms.form-dirty-guard**
- The tab-reload beforeunload leg (S1's aside) was not driven (it is a native prompt; the pin's describe.each covers it at the component layer).

**studio-authoring.flow-status-matches-runtime**
1. A flow authored over the API with `status:'draft'` is **enabled and bound** (_status {enabled:true,bound:true,status:'draft'}) and fires on a create (run_fcc42d7c). That is by design: the boot logs "draft flows still fire their triggers; set status: 'active' … or 'obsolete' to disable". "Created Off" therefore means `status:'obsolete'`; that is what the Studio switch writes (StudioDesignSurface toggleEnabled: active ↔ obsolete). The fixture text should say so for API authoring.
2. On the default boot, the schedule flow's header shows the enable switch green, labelled "Switched on", beside "Status: Not running here". The switch reflects `enabled` (true, which _status agrees with); the status word and the dot carry the binding. I do not read it as N0's "green On", but a reader of N0 could, so the clause could name the status pill and dot as the surfaces it means.
3. The launch entry showcase-scheduled-work-3778 has its own fixed port; this run used the same environment on runner port 41303.
